label: lunar occultation
definition: The passage of the Moon in front of a star or planet as seen by an observer. A solar eclipse is the special case in which the occulted body is the Sun.

label: shadow cylinder
definition: For a star at effectively infinite distance the Moon's shadow is a cylinder of radius $k$ rather than a cone, so on the fundamental plane it is a circle of fixed size whose centre moves with the Moon.

label: occultation elements
definition: The Besselian elements of a lunar occultation of a star, given once for the instant of conjunction in right ascension: the time $T_0$, the Greenwich hour angle $H$ of the star, $Y$, the hourly rates $x'$ and $y'$, and the star's right ascension and declination.

label: disappearance and reappearance (D, R)
definition: The two events of an ordinary occultation: the star vanishes at the Moon's leading limb (D) and returns at the trailing limb (R). Reports add the limb, so DD is a disappearance at the dark limb and RB a reappearance at the bright limb.

label: dark limb and bright limb
definition: The unlit and sunlit parts of the Moon's edge. Events at the dark limb are sharp and easy to time. Events at the bright limb are hidden by glare except for bright stars.

label: kn cos ψ
definition: The quantity in the Explanatory Supplement's prediction method equal to $k$ times the radial rate $n\cos\psi$ at which the observer's projection crosses the Moon's limb along the radius to the star. Timing errors scale as its inverse, so it tends to zero as an occultation becomes a graze.

label: grazing occultation
definition: An occultation seen from close to a limit line, where the star appears to skim the Moon's north or south edge and may disappear and reappear several times behind mountains and valleys.

label: northern and southern limit lines
definition: The two curves on the Earth's surface along which the star's track is tangent to the Moon's mean limb. Outside them there is no occultation. Near them a graze is seen.

label: limiting parallels
definition: The most northerly and most southerly latitudes from which a given occultation can be seen, published with the old prediction elements as a quick visibility test.

label: a and b coefficients
definition: The rates of change of a predicted occultation time with the observer's longitude and latitude, in minutes of time per degree, published with standard-station predictions so that nearby observers can correct the time.

label: cusp angle (CA)
definition: The angle around the Moon's limb from the nearer cusp to the point of an event, positive on the dark side and negative on the sunlit side, as used in IOTA and RASC predictions.

label: elevation correction (tan Z)
definition: The shift of a graze limit line on the ground for an observer above sea level, equal to the height times the tangent of the zenith distance and applied toward the Moon's azimuth.

label: Zodiacal Catalogue (ZC)
definition: Robertson's 1940 Catalog of 3539 Zodiacal Stars for the Equinox 1950.0, the standard list of brighter stars that the Moon can occult. Its numbers still name the stars in published predictions.

label: XZ catalogue
definition: The zodiacal star catalogue begun at the US Naval Observatory in 1977 for occultation predictions and reductions, covering 6 degrees 40 arcminutes either side of the ecliptic. The current version XZ80Q has 244,437 entries.

label: occultation residual (O−C)
definition: The computed angular distance of the star from the lunar limb at the observed time, in arcseconds, written $\Delta\sigma$ and positive outside the limb. It is the observed-minus-computed quantity of an occultation reduction.

label: personal equation
definition: The systematic delay between an event and a visual observer's timing of it, typically several tenths of a second, which reductions subtract.

label: occultation diffraction pattern
definition: The Fresnel fringes in a star's light just before it is cut off by the straight edge of the lunar limb. Their spacing of order 10 m at the Earth sweeps past the telescope in milliseconds, and their smoothing measures the star's angular diameter.

label: vector separation
definition: The component of a double star's separation along the direction in which the lunar limb moves across it, which is all that one occultation timing measures.

label: relative parallax
definition: The difference between the Moon's and a planet's horizontal parallaxes. Chauvenet uses it in place of the Moon's parallax to treat an occultation of a distant planet by the method for a star.

label: epoch propagation
definition: Moving a star's catalogue position, parallax and proper motion from the catalogue epoch to the date of an event, rigorously under uniform space motion, which needs the radial velocity for nearby fast stars.
